problem: Factories lose money when materials are missing, machines go down or staffing mismatches demand, and legacy ERPs with AI agents bolted on cannot reason over the underlying data.

founders.name: Christian Santos
previous_startups: Kinetic Labs (custom keyboard factory, ran six years per YC page)

founders.name: Lisa Mengotto
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder on company site; YC page names her in a photo caption.

technical_complexity.rationale: ERP breadth (demand planning, materials, maintenance, scheduling) is large for a small team, but modern LLM and ML tooling lowers the cost; integration with factory data is the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: ERPs lock in once data and processes migrate, but a brand-new product with one named customer has no moat yet.

market_need_then: Founders cite their own six years running a US factory; the company reports one named customer (Kinetic Labs) with a self-reported 22% higher operating margin.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, plain statements aimed at manufacturers; bold claims such as 'The Superintelligent OS'

brand_strength.rationale: New brand with no external press about it; name looks like 'organize' plus a suffix but no source explains it.

outcome_analysis: Organizely is a Fall 2026 YC company with no history to judge yet. Its edge is founders who ran a factory themselves and a claim of deployments in six states, but the only named customer is the founders' own prior company, and the AI-ERP field already has several funded rivals, so early traction needs independent customers.
